category: Descriptive Statistics II, Distance Measures & Uncertainty
description: Robust and alternative location and dispersion estimators, shape and dependence measures beyond Correlation, ranked statistics, cumulants and moments, the distance and dissimilarity functions shared by Nearest/FindClusters/DistanceMatrix, dynamic time warping, and the Around/Interval framework for computing with uncertainties and interval arithmetic.

tools.name: TrimmedMean
tools.description: Mean after discarding a fraction f (or {f1, f2} from each end) of the smallest and largest values - a robust location estimate; WinsorizedMean instead replaces the extremes by the nearest retained values, and TrimmedVariance / WinsorizedVariance are the dispersion analogues. Use them when outliers would distort Mean/Variance.
tools.usage:
TrimmedMean[list]
TrimmedMean[list, f]
TrimmedMean[list, {f1, f2}]
WinsorizedMean[list, f]
TrimmedVariance[list, f]
WinsorizedVariance[list, f]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Fraction trimmed from each end (default 0.05 for the one-argument form).

tools.example:
data = {1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 100};
{Mean[data], TrimmedMean[data, 0.125], WinsorizedMean[data, 0.125], Median[data]}

tools.name: HarmonicMean
tools.description: Pythagorean means: HarmonicMean (rates, e.g. average speed over equal distances), GeometricMean (growth factors, ratios), ContraharmonicMean, and the classic Mean; RootMeanSquare gives the RMS value used for signal amplitude and error metrics. All are Listable over columns of matrices and accept symbolic input.
tools.usage:
HarmonicMean[list]
GeometricMean[list]
ContraharmonicMean[list]
RootMeanSquare[list]
tools.example:
GeometricMean[{1.05, 1.10, 0.95}] - 1 (* average growth rate *)
HarmonicMean[{60, 40}] (* average speed for equal distances: 48 *)
RootMeanSquare[Table[Sin[t], {t, 0, 2 Pi, 0.001}]] (* ~0.707 *)

tools.name: BiweightLocation
tools.description: Tukey's biweight location estimator (highly robust, efficient for near-normal data) with BiweightMidvariance its scale counterpart; SpatialMedian is the multivariate median (geometric median minimizing summed distances) and CentralFeature the data point closest to it. Use them for robust centres of multivariate or contaminated data.
tools.usage:
BiweightLocation[list]
BiweightLocation[list, c]
BiweightMidvariance[list]
SpatialMedian[points]
CentralFeature[points]
CentralFeature[points, DistanceFunction -> ManhattanDistance]

tools.name: MeanDeviation
tools.description: Dispersion measures: MeanDeviation (mean absolute deviation from the mean), MedianDeviation (median absolute deviation, MAD - the standard robust scale), QuartileDeviation (half the interquartile range), InterquartileRange, and the highly robust QnDispersion and SnDispersion estimators of Rousseeuw and Croux. Scale MedianDeviation by 1.4826 to estimate sigma for normal data.
tools.usage:
MeanDeviation[list]
MedianDeviation[list]
QuartileDeviation[list]
InterquartileRange[list]
QnDispersion[list]
SnDispersion[list]

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Numeric data (matrices are processed by column).

tools.example:
data = RandomVariate[NormalDistribution[0, 2], 1000];
{StandardDeviation[data], 1.4826 MedianDeviation[data], InterquartileRange[data]/1.349, QnDispersion[data]}

tools.name: QuartileSkewness
tools.description: Robust (Bowley) skewness based on quartiles, complementing the moment-based Skewness/Kurtosis (listed); Entropy computes the Shannon entropy of a discrete data set or of a distribution (base e by default), a measure of dispersion for categorical data. Both are useful descriptive summaries in exploratory analysis.
tools.usage:
QuartileSkewness[list]
Entropy[list]
Entropy[b, list]
Entropy[dist]
tools.example:
QuartileSkewness[RandomVariate[ExponentialDistribution[1], 500]]
Entropy[2, Characters["mississippi"]] (* bits per character *)
Entropy[NormalDistribution[0, 1]] (* 1/2 (1 + Log[2 Pi]) *)

tools.name: SpearmanRho
tools.description: Rank-based dependence measures: SpearmanRho (rank correlation), KendallTau (concordance), GoodmanKruskalGamma and BlomqvistBeta (medial correlation), HoeffdingD (detects any dependence, not just monotone) and AbsoluteCorrelation (uncentred correlation). They are the descriptive counterparts of the hypothesis tests SpearmanRankTest etc. (listed) and are robust to outliers and nonlinearity.
tools.usage:
SpearmanRho[x, y]
SpearmanRho[matrix]
KendallTau[x, y]
GoodmanKruskalGamma[x, y]
BlomqvistBeta[x, y]
HoeffdingD[x, y]
AbsoluteCorrelation[x, y]

parameters.name: x, y
parameters.description: Equal-length data lists (or a matrix for pairwise measures).

tools.name: RankedMin
tools.description: RankedMin[list, n] gives the n-th smallest element and RankedMax the n-th largest (order statistics), the fast alternative to Sort[list][[n]]; Quantile/Quartiles (listed) interpolate between them. Useful for percentile-style thresholds and k-th nearest distances.
tools.usage:
RankedMin[list, n]
RankedMax[list, n]
tools.example:
RankedMax[{5, 1, 9, 7}, 2] (* 7 *)
kthDist = RankedMin[EuclideanDistance[p, #] & /@ pts, 4] (* 4th nearest neighbour distance *)

tools.name: Cumulant
tools.description: Cumulant[data, r] / Cumulant[dist, r] gives the r-th cumulant (kappa_1 mean, kappa_2 variance, kappa_3 third central moment, ...) and FactorialMoment the r-th factorial moment (used for count distributions); with Moment and CentralMoment (listed) plus the generating functions they cover all moment-type summaries. Symbolic distributions give closed forms.
tools.usage:
Cumulant[list, r]
Cumulant[dist, r]
FactorialMoment[list, r]
FactorialMoment[dist, r]
tools.example:
Cumulant[PoissonDistribution[lambda], 4] (* lambda: all cumulants equal lambda *)
FactorialMoment[PoissonDistribution[lambda], 3] (* lambda^3 *)
Cumulant[data, 3]/Cumulant[data, 2]^(3/2) (* skewness *)

tools.name: EuclideanDistance
tools.description: Vector distance functions accepted by Nearest, FindClusters, DistanceMatrix, ClusteringTree and as DistanceFunction options: EuclideanDistance, SquaredEuclideanDistance, NormalizedSquaredEuclideanDistance, ManhattanDistance (L1), ChessboardDistance (L-infinity), CosineDistance (1 - cosine similarity), CorrelationDistance (1 - correlation), BrayCurtisDistance and CanberraDistance. All work on numeric vectors and symbolically.
tools.usage:
EuclideanDistance[u, v]
SquaredEuclideanDistance[u, v]
NormalizedSquaredEuclideanDistance[u, v]
ManhattanDistance[u, v]
ChessboardDistance[u, v]
CosineDistance[u, v]
CorrelationDistance[u, v]
BrayCurtisDistance[u, v]
CanberraDistance[u, v]
Nearest[data, x, DistanceFunction -> CosineDistance]
tools.example:
CosineDistance[{1, 0, 1}, {1, 1, 0}] (* 1/2 *)
FindClusters[vectors, 3, DistanceFunction -> ManhattanDistance]
DistanceMatrix[pts, DistanceFunction -> ChessboardDistance]

tools.name: JaccardDissimilarity
tools.description: Dissimilarity measures for Boolean/binary vectors: JaccardDissimilarity, DiceDissimilarity, MatchingDissimilarity (simple matching), RogersTanimotoDissimilarity, RussellRaoDissimilarity, SokalSneathDissimilarity, YuleDissimilarity; and BinaryDistance (0 if identical, 1 otherwise) for arbitrary expressions. Use them for set-membership fingerprints, presence/absence ecology data and molecular fingerprints.
tools.usage:
JaccardDissimilarity[u, v]
DiceDissimilarity[u, v]
MatchingDissimilarity[u, v]
RogersTanimotoDissimilarity[u, v]
RussellRaoDissimilarity[u, v]
SokalSneathDissimilarity[u, v]
YuleDissimilarity[u, v]
BinaryDistance[u, v]

parameters.name: u, v
parameters.description: Boolean vectors (True/False or 0/1) of equal length.

tools.example:
JaccardDissimilarity[{1, 1, 0, 0}, {1, 0, 1, 0}] (* 2/3 *)
FindClusters[fingerprints, DistanceFunction -> JaccardDissimilarity]

tools.name: WarpingDistance
tools.description: Dynamic time warping distance between two sequences (of numbers, vectors or any objects with a DistanceFunction), allowing non-linear time alignment, with window constraints ("SlantedBand", "ItakuraParallelogram") for speed; CanonicalWarpingDistance normalizes by path length, WarpingCorrespondence returns the alignment path. Standard for comparing time series, gestures and speech features of different lengths.
tools.usage:
WarpingDistance[s1, s2]
WarpingDistance[s1, s2, DistanceFunction -> EuclideanDistance]
WarpingDistance[s1, s2, Method -> {"SlantedBand", 10}]
CanonicalWarpingDistance[s1, s2]
WarpingCorrespondence[s1, s2]

parameters.name: s1, s2
parameters.description: Sequences (lists of numbers or vectors, TimeSeries, Audio).

tools.name: DistanceMatrix
tools.description: Computes the matrix of pairwise distances within a set or between two sets (points, strings, images, expressions) with any DistanceFunction, returning a dense (optionally sparse or packed) matrix used by hierarchical clustering, MDS-style embeddings and TSP; DistanceFunction is the shared option name across Nearest, FindClusters, ClusteringTree, Dendrogram, DimensionReduce and FindShortestTour. MeanShift shifts points toward local density maxima (mean-shift clustering/smoothing).
tools.usage:
DistanceMatrix[{p1, p2, ...}]
DistanceMatrix[{p1, ...}, {q1, ...}]
DistanceMatrix[pts, DistanceFunction -> ManhattanDistance]
DistanceMatrix[strings, DistanceFunction -> EditDistance]
MeanShift[pts, r]
MeanShift[pts, r, MaxIterations -> 20]
tools.example:
dm = DistanceMatrix[RandomReal[1, {8, 2}]];
MatrixPlot[dm]
ClusteringTree[dm] (* accepts a distance matrix *)
DistanceMatrix[{"kitten", "sitting", "mitten"}, DistanceFunction -> EditDistance]

tools.name: Around
tools.description: Around[x, dx] represents a value with uncertainty (standard deviation dx, or asymmetric {dminus, dplus}, or an Interval); arithmetic and most numeric functions propagate uncertainties by linear error propagation (assuming independence), plots draw error bars/bands automatically, and Around[data] summarizes a sample as mean ± standard error. It is the standard type for measured quantities with errors, replacing ad-hoc {value, error} pairs.
tools.usage:
Around[x, dx]
Around[x, {dminus, dplus}]
Around[x, Interval[{a, b}]]
Around[list] (* mean and standard error of the list *)
Around[Quantity[9.81, "m/s^2"], Quantity[0.02, "m/s^2"]]
a["Value"]
a["Uncertainty"]
a["Interval"]
tools.example:
L = Around[1.20, 0.01]; T = Around[2.20, 0.02];
g = 4 Pi^2 L/T^2 (* Around[9.79, 0.20] *)
ListPlot[Table[Around[Sin[x], 0.1], {x, 0, 6, 0.5}]] (* error bars *)
Around[{2.1, 2.3, 1.9, 2.2}]
tools.notes: Propagation is first order and assumes independent uncertainties; use VectorAround for correlated components. Introduced in 12.0.

tools.name: MeanAround
tools.description: MeanAround[data] gives the (weighted) mean of a list of numbers or Around values as an Around with the standard error of the mean, treating individual uncertainties as weights; AroundReplace substitutes Around values into an expression and propagates errors through it (with correlations handled), and VectorAround represents vectors with a covariance matrix or correlation. Use them to combine repeated measurements and to propagate errors through fitted models.
tools.usage:
MeanAround[{x1, x2, ...}]
MeanAround[{Around[x1, d1], Around[x2, d2], ...}]
AroundReplace[expr, {a -> Around[1, 0.1], b -> Around[2, 0.2]}]
AroundReplace[expr, {{a, b} -> VectorAround[{1, 2}, cov]}]
VectorAround[{x1, x2}, {d1, d2}]
VectorAround[{x1, x2}, covmatrix]

tools.name: Interval
tools.description: Interval[{a, b}] represents a closed real interval (unions of several allowed) with rigorous interval arithmetic: arithmetic, elementary functions, Min/Max, IntervalMemberQ, IntervalIntersection and IntervalUnion all produce enclosures of the true result. Used for guaranteed bounds, root isolation (Reduce over intervals), tolerance analysis and as the input form of Around and DistributionDomain.
tools.usage:
Interval[{a, b}]
Interval[{a1, b1}, {a2, b2}]
Interval[{1, 2}] + Interval[{-1, 1}]
Sin[Interval[{0, Pi}]]
IntervalMemberQ[int, x]
IntervalMemberQ[int1, int2]
IntervalIntersection[int1, int2]
IntervalUnion[int1, int2]
Min[int]
Max[int]
tools.example:
Interval[{1, 2}]^2 - 3 Interval[{1, 2}] (* Interval[{-5, 1}] *)
IntervalMemberQ[Interval[{0, 1}], 0.5] (* True *)
x = Interval[{0.1, 0.2}]; 1/x (* {5, 10} *)
tools.notes: Interval arithmetic over-estimates when a variable appears several times (dependency problem); rewrite expressions or use CenteredInterval for tighter complex enclosures.

tools.name: CenteredInterval
tools.description: CenteredInterval[c, r] represents a real or complex interval as centre ± radius (a disc for complex values), an alternative interval-arithmetic type (13.0+) that supports complex numbers and arbitrary-precision centre values; CenteredInterval[x] for an approximate number encloses its error bounds. Used for validated numerics and rigorous function evaluation.
tools.usage:
CenteredInterval[c, r]
CenteredInterval[Interval[{a, b}]]
CenteredInterval[x] (* from an approximate number *)
CenteredInterval[1 + I, 0.1]
Exp[CenteredInterval[1, 0.01]]

tools.name: WeightedData
tools.description: Represents a weighted sample: Mean, Variance, Median, Quantile, Histogram, EstimatedDistribution, SmoothKernelDistribution and hypothesis tests all honour the weights. Use it for survey weights, importance sampling and pre-binned data instead of expanding samples by hand; EventData is the analogue for censored survival data used by SurvivalModelFit.
tools.usage:
WeightedData[{x1, x2, ...}, {w1, w2, ...}]
WeightedData[data, f] (* weights from a function of the values *)
Mean[wd]
Quantile[wd, 0.9]
EstimatedDistribution[wd, NormalDistribution[m, s]]
EventData[times, censoringIndicators]

tools.name: WinsorizedMean
tools.description: Mean computed after replacing the fraction f of smallest and largest values by the nearest retained values (Winsorizing), a robust estimator that keeps the sample size unlike TrimmedMean; WinsorizedVariance is its dispersion counterpart.
tools.usage:
WinsorizedMean[list]
WinsorizedMean[list, f]
WinsorizedMean[list, {f1, f2}]
WinsorizedVariance[list, f]
tools.example: WinsorizedMean[{1, 2, 3, 4, 100}, 0.2] (* 3.2: 100 replaced by 4 *)

tools.name: GeometricMean
tools.description: The n-th root of the product of n positive numbers - the right average for growth factors, ratios and log-normally distributed quantities; equals Exp[Mean[Log[data]]]. Listable over matrix columns.
tools.usage: GeometricMean[list]
tools.example:
GeometricMean[{1.05, 1.10, 0.95}] - 1 (* average annual growth *)
GeometricMean[{{1, 4}, {9, 16}}] (* {3, 8} by column *)

tools.name: InterquartileRange
tools.description: Difference between the third and first quartiles (with Quantile-method options), the standard robust spread used in box plots and outlier rules (1.5 IQR); QuartileDeviation is half of it.
tools.usage:
InterquartileRange[list]
InterquartileRange[list, {{a, b}, {c, d}}] (* quantile definition *)
InterquartileRange[dist]

tools.name: KendallTau
tools.description: Kendall's tau rank correlation coefficient (concordant minus discordant pairs, normalized), a robust measure of monotone association less sensitive to outliers than Pearson correlation; KendallTauTest (listed among tests) gives the p-value.
tools.usage:
KendallTau[x, y]
KendallTau[matrix]

tools.name: RankedMax
tools.description: Gives the n-th largest element of a list (order statistic from the top), the fast partial-sort alternative to Sort[list][[-n]]; RankedMin is the mirror image.
tools.usage: RankedMax[list, n]
tools.example:
RankedMax[{5, 1, 9, 7}, 2] (* 7 *)
secondBest = RankedMax[scores, 2]

tools.name: ManhattanDistance
tools.description: L1 (city-block) distance, the sum of absolute coordinate differences; less sensitive to outlying coordinates than EuclideanDistance and the natural metric for grid movement and sparse data. Accepted wherever DistanceFunction is an option.
tools.usage:
ManhattanDistance[u, v]
Nearest[pts, p, DistanceFunction -> ManhattanDistance]
tools.example: ManhattanDistance[{1, 2}, {4, 6}] (* 7 *)

tools.name: ChessboardDistance
tools.description: L-infinity (Chebyshev) distance, the maximum absolute coordinate difference - the number of king moves on a chessboard; used for tolerance checks where every coordinate must be within a bound and in image morphology.
tools.usage: ChessboardDistance[u, v]
tools.example:
ChessboardDistance[{1, 2}, {4, 6}] (* 4 *)
Select[pts, ChessboardDistance[#, target] <= 0.01 &]

tools.name: CosineDistance
tools.description: 1 minus the cosine of the angle between two vectors, a scale-invariant dissimilarity that depends only on direction - the standard metric for text/feature embeddings, term-frequency vectors and recommendation similarity.
tools.usage:
CosineDistance[u, v]
Nearest[embeddings -> "Index", q, DistanceFunction -> CosineDistance]
tools.example:
CosineDistance[{1, 0, 1}, {1, 1, 0}] (* 1/2 *)
CosineDistance[{1, 2}, {2, 4}] (* 0: same direction *)

tools.name: CorrelationDistance
tools.description: 1 minus the Pearson correlation of two vectors (equivalently the cosine distance of the mean-centred vectors), used to cluster time series or gene-expression profiles by shape regardless of offset and scale.
tools.usage:
CorrelationDistance[u, v]
FindClusters[series, DistanceFunction -> CorrelationDistance]
tools.example:
CorrelationDistance[{1, 2, 3}, {2, 4, 6}] (* 0 *)
CorrelationDistance[{1, 2, 3}, {3, 2, 1}] (* 2 *)

tools.name: IntervalMemberQ
tools.description: Tests whether a number (or a whole interval) lies inside an Interval object; IntervalIntersection and IntervalUnion combine intervals, and Min/Max give their endpoints. These are the set operations of interval arithmetic used for range checks and root isolation.
tools.usage:
IntervalMemberQ[interval, x]
IntervalMemberQ[interval1, interval2]
IntervalIntersection[int1, int2, ...]
IntervalUnion[int1, int2, ...]
tools.example:
IntervalMemberQ[Interval[{0, 1}], 0.5] (* True *)
IntervalIntersection[Interval[{0, 2}], Interval[{1, 3}]] (* Interval[{1, 2}] *)

tools.name: VectorAround
tools.description: Represents a vector of approximate values with uncertainties that may be correlated (given a covariance matrix or correlation), so that functions of several fitted parameters propagate errors correctly; typically built from a model's "BestFitParameters" and "CovarianceMatrix" and used inside AroundReplace.
tools.usage:
VectorAround[{x1, x2, ...}, {d1, d2, ...}]
VectorAround[{x1, x2, ...}, covmatrix]
VectorAround[{x1, x2}, {d1, d2}, rho]
va["Values"]
va["Covariance"]

tools.name: AroundReplace
tools.description: Substitutes Around (or VectorAround) values into an expression and propagates the uncertainties through it to first order, taking correlations into account when the same Around appears several times - unlike plain ReplaceAll, which would treat repeated occurrences as independent.
tools.usage:
AroundReplace[expr, {x -> Around[1, 0.1]}]
AroundReplace[expr, {{a, b} -> VectorAround[vals, cov]}]
tools.example: AroundReplace[x^2 - x, {x -> Around[2, 0.1]}] (* Around[2, 0.3]: correlated, unlike (Around[2,0.1])^2 - Around[2,0.1] *)
